<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix canonical tiering storage sizing when TP exceeds the number of KV heads, so replicated GQA caches can be persisted and reused across TP sizes. Discovered during the chunked-local work in #61886 and reproduced independently with full attention.

Follow-up: #62162 enables chunked-local canonical offload on top of this fix.

## Claims

- Canonical storage counts unique KV-head copies rather than physical TP ranks.
- Worker mmap population stays within the deduplicated row.
- Default CPU offloading, noncanonical layouts and existing MLA replication semantics are preserved.

## Validation

**Current head `05c4d90acb` (2026-11-02): 229 passed, 12 skipped** on macOS CPU. Review cleanup reduces the config matrix to four representative layouts, moves population-slot/bounds checks into the existing worker-placement test, and removes the requested upgrade-doc section. Production code and FS round-trip/isolation tests are unchanged. Skips: 11 native `fs_io_C` cases and one `/dev/shm` case. Pre-commit, including mypy, passed.

Current Mac mutation checks: restoring physical-TP sizing gives **4 failures / 3 passes** across the four config and three FS round-trip cases; restoring physical population ranks gives **2 failures / 1 pass**; restoring format v1 gives **2 isolation failures**. All mutations were reverted.

Previous Linux validation at `ab657e4894`: **225 passed, zero skipped**, with native `fs_io_C` and O_DIRECT on ext4 (Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.12.12 / PyTorch 2.14.0+cpu).

The extended FS tests use production configuration sizing, actual files, independent writer/reader managers and byte-exact checks for **1 KV head, TP1→TP2 and TP2→TP1**. NHD/HND upgrade tests check cross-version misses, same-key coexistence and unchanged file contents.

Linux regression sensitivity at `ab657e4894`: restoring physical-TP sizing yields **2 failures / 1 pass** (native read error and excess persisted bytes); restoring v1 yields **2 failures** (HIT instead of MISS). All temporary changes were reverted. These tests run in the existing Buildkite `v1-kv-offload` step; they require only CPU, although that CI runner is GPU-hosted.

Linux command below uses the tested host's virtualenv/cache paths. For the current Mac run, the same suites used `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p cpu_only`, with offline OPT config and the existing external `cpu_only` plugin marking accelerator cleanup as unsupported. The plugin does not skip test bodies.

```bash
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 PYTHONPATH=.
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 HF_HOME=/data/kv-review-hf
export HF_HUB_CACHE="$HF_HOME/hub" HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE="$HF_HOME/hub"
/data/kv-review-py312/bin/python -m pytest -q -rs --tb=short \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_canonical_mapping.py
```

<details>
<summary>Historical dual-GPU validation — commit a99a46153a</summary>

On 2× RTX 5090, tiny Llama4 full attention (1 KV head, FP16/eager/Triton) passed 5 inference processes: a no-offload TP1 reference and independent TP1↔TP2 filesystem producer/reader pairs. Both directions hit 240/240 contexts in cold/reload phases. Maximum absolute logprob delta across all 512 vocabulary entries was 0.002874, below the 0.005 tolerance; FS reads and CPU→GPU counters confirmed actual reuse.

[Historical commands, logs and environment](https://github.com/xiaoba17/vllm/tree/10218a6806b5fff79919eb02fff11c265d2c41de). This outside-CI run used native-extension baseline `8e25bbca19` and random tiny weights: it validates execution/cache correctness, not model quality or performance.

</details>

**Linux native/O_DIRECT and GPU inference have not been rerun at the current head.**

## Details

Canonical mappings already deduplicate replicated GQA heads, but tiering allocated rows using physical world size. With one KV head, TP1 and TP2 therefore shared a storage namespace while expecting different file sizes (4096 versus 8192 bytes in the minimal Linux reproducer), causing the TP2 reader to reject TP1 files.

Carry the certified canonical replication factor into tiering's copy-count calculation and map population ranks to unique head slots. The canonical mapping's rank and writer-selection logic remains unchanged. Regression mutations removing either the sizing correction or the rank correction fail the targeted tests.

Canonical format **v2** isolates compact files from v1 readers for every TP size, preventing old readers from treating new files as truncated and deleting them. Compatible v2 TP1/TP2 instances still share caches; NHD/HND remain separate. All v1 canonical caches become cold after upgrading, even where row size did not change. No automatic migration or deletion is performed; noncanonical namespaces are unchanged.

Duplicate-work check: #56953 concerns per-group slot sizing, whereas this fixes replicated TP copies; #60782 refactors shared-region classes without changing their sizing semantics. Neither implements this fix. Related tracking issue: #61886 (not closed by this PR).

AI assistance: Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and PR preparation. I have reviewed the changes and completed the relevant tests and behavioral validation.

+def test_canonical_fs_upgrade_isolates_legacy_files(
+    tmp_path, monkeypatch, layout, family

+    """Rolling-upgrade peers cannot overwrite or delete the other format's files."""
+    new_spec = _canonical_gqa_spec(2, layout)
+    # Reproduce the old TP2 allocation and version without changing FS behavior.
+    old_spec = TieringOffloadingSpec(replace(new_spec.config, canonical_kv_replicas=1))
+    tensors = [
+        _page_aligned_zero_tensor(4, spec.kv_bytes_per_chunk, torch.uint8)
+        for spec in (old_spec, new_spec)
+    ]
+    tensors[0][0].fill_(17)
+    tensors[1][0].fill_(93)
+    tiers = []
+    try:
+        versions = (1, canonical_mapping.CANONICAL_FORMAT_VERSION)
+        for version, spec, tensor in zip(versions, (old_spec, new_spec), tensors):
+            with monkeypatch.context() as patch:
+                patch.setattr(canonical_mapping, "CANONICAL_FORMAT_VERSION", version)
+                tiers.append(
+                    FileSystemTierManager(
+                        offloading_spec=spec,
+                        primary_kv_view=memoryview(tensor.numpy()),
+                        tier_type="fs",
+                        root_dir=str(tmp_path),
+                    )
+                )
+        old, new = tiers
+        # Each reader misses the other version's key; both files remain intact.
+        for i, tier in enumerate(tiers):
+            tier.submit_store(make_job(i, [key(i)], [0]))
+            results = drain(tier)
+            assert len(results) == 1 and results[0].success
+            assert lookup_and_wait(tiers[1 - i], [key(i)]) == [LookupResult.MISS]
+        for i, tier in enumerate(tiers):
+            # Write the same logical key into the other namespace, too.
+            tier.submit_store(make_job(10 + i, [key(1 - i)], [0]))
+            results = drain(tier)
+            assert len(results) == 1 and results[0].success
+            tier.submit_load(make_job(20 + i, [key(i)], [1], is_promotion=True))
+            results = drain(tier)
+            assert len(results) == 1 and results[0].success
+            assert torch.equal(tensors[i][1], tensors[i][0])
+        for i, tier in enumerate(tiers):
+            for k in (key(0), key(1)):
+                assert Path(tier.file_mapper.get_file_name(k)).read_bytes() == (
+                    tensors[i][0].numpy().tobytes()
+                )
+        assert old.file_mapper.fields["canonical_format"] == f"v1-{family}"
+        assert new.file_mapper.fields["canonical_format"] == f"v2-{family}"
+        assert old.file_mapper.base_path != new.file_mapper.base_path
+    finally:
+        for tier in tiers:
+            tier.shutdown()
